$comment: The eval cases, written from the Policy files and World/world.json before the first run, and never reworded to make them pass: a case that fails stays failing with a knownMiss note until the prompt or tools are fixed. The fields are documented on EvalCase.

turns: who pays for the return shipping if I send something back for a refund?
cases.reference: For a refund, a $6.95 return label fee is deducted from your refund (Returns Policy › Return shipping cost). Return shipping is free for exchanges and for defective or wrong items. Original shipping charges are not refunded unless the item was defective or we sent the wrong item.
rubric: Says a $6.95 return label fee is deducted from the refund
Does not say that return shipping for a refund is free

turns: can I return a bike helmet I've already worn outside?
cases.reference: No. Bike helmets cannot be returned once worn outside, or after any impact (Returns Exceptions › Helmets). Only unworn helmets with tags and packaging can be returned, within 60 days. If the helmet was in a crash, it may qualify for the Crash Replacement discount (Warranty Overview).
rubric: Says a helmet that has been worn outside cannot be returned
Does not say the worn helmet can be returned under the standard 60-day window

turns: can I swap my boots for a bigger size?
cases.reference: Yes. You can exchange an item for a different size of the same product within 60 days of the order date (Exchanges › What you can exchange), as long as it meets the return condition rules; boots must have been worn indoors only (Returns Exceptions › Footwear). Your first exchange per item is free.
rubric: Says the boots can be exchanged for a different size of the same product
Gives the 60-day limit, counted from the order date
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 1/3 samples. In 2 samples Haiku called no search_policies: it asked for the order details instead, so it cited nothing and gave no exchange rule or 60-day limit. The golden set records this question as a semantic retrieval miss; here retrieval was never tried.

turns: can I change the shipping address on an order I've already placed?
mustCite: Order Cancellation and Changes › Changing an order
cases.reference: No. An order cannot be changed once it is placed, including its shipping address (Order Cancellation and Changes › Changing an order). To change it, cancel the order while that is still possible (until it is paid) and place a new one.
rubric: Says the shipping address of a placed order cannot be changed
Says to cancel the order while it can still be cancelled and place a new one

turns: my parcel never arrived, what should I do?
mustCite: Order Status and Tracking › Late, lost or damaged parcels
cases.reference: If your parcel has not arrived 5 business days after the latest estimated delivery date, contact us and we will open a claim with the carrier; we will send a free replacement or refund you in full, including shipping (Order Status and Tracking › Late, lost or damaged parcels).
rubric: Says to contact AdventureWorks once the parcel is 5 business days past the latest estimated date, and that a claim is opened with the carrier
Says the outcome is a free replacement or a full refund including shipping
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 0/3 samples. Haiku never called search_policies: it asked for the order number instead of stating the Late, lost or damaged parcels rule (5 business days, carrier claim, free replacement or full refund).

turns: is there an extra charge to ship a snowboard?
cases.reference: Yes. Each snowboard has a $25 oversized surcharge, per item, and it applies even when Standard shipping is free over $75 (Oversized Shipping › Surcharge). Oversized items ship by Standard only.
rubric: Says there is a $25 oversized surcharge per snowboard
Does not say free shipping over $75 removes the surcharge

turns: can I pay with PayPal?
mustCite: Payments and Billing › Accepted payment methods
cases.reference: No, PayPal is not accepted. AdventureWorks accepts Visa, Mastercard and American Express credit and debit cards (Payments and Billing › Accepted payment methods). Gift cards can be used alongside a card.
rubric: Says PayPal is not accepted
Names Visa, Mastercard and American Express (Amex) as the accepted cards

turns: do your gift cards expire?
mustCite: Promotions and Gift Cards › Gift cards
cases.reference: No. AdventureWorks gift cards never expire and have no fees (Promotions and Gift Cards › Gift cards).
rubric: Says gift cards never expire
Does not state an expiry period or a fee for gift cards

turns: how much is shipping to Canada?
cases.reference: To Canada, Standard shipping is $14.95 (5–10 business days) and Expedited is $29.95 (3–5 business days); Next day is not available, and free shipping over $75 does not apply to Canada (Shipping Destinations › Canada). Import duties and taxes are collected on delivery.
rubric: Gives Standard at $14.95 and Expedited at $29.95 for Canada
Does not say free shipping over $75 applies to Canada

turns: how much do I need to spend to get free shipping?
mustCite: Shipping Options and Costs › Free shipping over $75
cases.reference: Standard shipping is free when your order total is over $75, after discounts and before tax (Shipping Options and Costs › Free shipping over $75). It does not apply to Expedited or Next day, or to the oversized surcharge on skis and snowboards.
rubric: Says Standard shipping is free on orders over $75
Does not say Expedited or Next day shipping becomes free over $75
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 0/3 samples. The rule was right every time ($75, Standard only, after discounts and before tax) and came from search_policies, but no answer cited a Policy Section, so Citations present failed.

turns: what size hiking boots should I get compared to my everyday shoes?
mustCite: Sizing Guide: Jackets and Footwear › Choosing the right footwear size
cases.reference: Go half a size up from your everyday shoes, so you have about a thumb's width of space in front of your longest toe (Sizing Guide: Jackets and Footwear › Choosing the right footwear size). Try them on indoors with the socks you will wear outside.
rubric: Says to go half a size up from everyday shoes
Does not recommend going down a size or the same size for hiking boots

turns: how do I measure my head for a bike helmet?
mustCite: Sizing Guide: Helmets, Packs and Harnesses › Bike helmets
cases.reference: Measure around your head about 1 inch (2.5 cm) above your eyebrows, keeping the tape level (Sizing Guide: Helmets, Packs and Harnesses › Bike helmets). S is 51–55 cm, M 55–59 cm and L 59–63 cm; between sizes, choose the smaller size and use the fit dial.
rubric: Says to measure around the head about 1 inch (2.5 cm) above the eyebrows with the tape level
Any sizes or between-sizes advice given matches the Policy (S 51–55 cm, M 55–59 cm, L 59–63 cm; choose the smaller size when between sizes)
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 0/3 samples. Haiku never called search_policies and declined to explain how to measure, as if helmet sizing were outside its scope.

turns: I'm 5'8" and an intermediate skier, what ski length should I get?
mustCite: Sizing Guide: Skis and Snowboards › Ski length by height and ability
cases.reference: For 5'8" (173 cm) at intermediate level, the guide suggests 165–170 cm skis (Sizing Guide: Skis and Snowboards › Ski length by height and ability). Go a size longer if you weigh more than average for your height, or shorter if less.
rubric: Recommends 165–170 cm

turns: my helmet was in a crash, can I get a replacement?
mustCite: Warranty Overview › Crash Replacement for helmets
cases.reference: A helmet that has been in any impact must be replaced, even if it looks fine. Accidents aren't covered by warranty, but within 3 years of the order date AdventureWorks offers 30% off a replacement helmet from the same brand; contact us with your order number and a photo of the damaged helmet (Warranty Overview › Crash Replacement for helmets).
rubric: Says there is 30% off a replacement helmet from the same brand within 3 years of the order date
Does not say the crash damage is covered by the warranty or that the replacement is free
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 0/3 samples. Haiku never called search_policies: it asked for the order number and purchase date, and never mentioned the 30% Crash Replacement discount.

turns: the sole of my boot is coming off, is that a defect?
cases.reference: Yes. Soles separating from the upper is a defect, not normal wear, so it is covered by the warranty (Defects vs Normal Wear › Footwear). Within 60 days of the order date AdventureWorks handles it with a free return; after that the claim goes to the brand.
rubric: Says a sole separating from the upper is a defect
Does not call it normal wear
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 1/3 samples. In 2 samples Haiku called no search_policies and put off the answer until it had the order number and purchase date.

The Frostbite Insulated Jacket has the standard 60-day window, until December 30, 2026 (Returns Policy › Return window).
rubric: Gives a separate Return Window per item: 30 days for the GPS watch and 60 days for the jacket

turns: I want to return the helmet from order 102, how do I do that?
mustCite: Returns Policy › How to start a return
cases.reference: Order 102 (the Trailblazer Bike Helmet) is still awaiting validation, so it hasn't shipped yet, and you can only return an order once its status is Shipped (Returns Policy › How to start a return). Because it hasn't been paid yet, you can cancel it instead from My orders (Order Cancellation and Changes › When you can cancel).
rubric: Says order 102 can't be returned yet because it hasn't shipped (it is awaiting validation)
Suggests cancelling the order instead, since it has not been paid yet
Does not give return steps or a return window as if the helmet could be returned now
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 0/3 samples. Haiku treated the AwaitingValidation order as returnable now (the 60-day window to December 29, 2026, plus return steps), didn't cite Returns Policy › How to start a return, and didn't suggest cancelling. One sample framed the steps as applying once it ships, which still fails rubric item 3. Ticket 03's first tracer run made the same miss.

turns: can I still return the boots from order 103?
cases.reference: No. Order 103 was placed on July 15, 2026, and the Wanderer Black Hiking Boots had a 60-day return window from the order date (Returns Policy › Return window; Returns Exceptions › Footwear), which ended on September 13, 2026. Today is November 1, 2026, so they can no longer be returned. If they are defective, a warranty claim may still be possible (Warranty Overview).
rubric: Says the boots can no longer be returned because the return window has passed
Says the window was 60 days from the order date (July 15, 2026), ending on September 13, 2026
Cites a Policy Section that gives the 60-day window for the boots
cases.knownMiss: Baseline 2026-11-09, 1/3 samples. Every sample said the boots can no longer be returned (60 days from July 15, 2026), but 2 samples left out the September 13, 2026 end date that rubric item 2 asks for.
